mathematical_repairs: Ideal inclusion preserves log-ideal-function order after two sign reversals; degree-m additive weights are the integers -k and their normalized contributions are -k/m.

Relative generation on the affine base concerns the sheaf on S. The original degree-k evaluation source is correct: lower-degree sections are already identified inside its tensor product over k[t]; the proof now explains this, without claiming a defect in the original formula.
Envelope comparison corrects the actual Q-line bundle in Picard group, using an ample N=L-(1-delta)Li-deltaE and its zero section function, rather than merely correcting a numerical class.

Veronese scaling, normal codimension-one membership, proper valuative lifts and support-versus-centre distinctions are explicit. A homogeneous bounded PL function on the projective analytification is zero.
Plane-example coefficient ideals, Newton polyhedron of J1, infinite-value formula and finite-stage agreement locus are corrected. The actual plane-example gap is bounded by 2/m uniformly.
Unbounded discrepancy estimates prove no uniform bound, not failure of actual uniform convergence. Proper-support evaluation discontinuity concerns a different topology.
The Gauss discrepancy proof uses a smooth neighbourhood of the divisor generic point on a normal model and a local toroidal construction; no global resolution in arbitrary characteristic is assumed.
Multiplier containment chooses a stabilizing q divisible by m. Unsupported Frobenius-root factorization and rounding sketches are replaced by the precise named asymptotic subadditivity input.

Canton valuation estimate is stated for smooth finite-type schemes over the given algebraically closed field; trace levels start at e=1 and the correct citation is Definition 3.3 plus Proposition 4.1.
General moving-class closure needs class convergence and a nontrivial limit; nef orientation additionally supplies a fixed-class-tail proof, rather than being a necessary general closure hypothesis.

A positive-genus curve with very ample L and zero obstacle has Bm=O, um=Q=0 and nonzero presented class drift. This supplies the missing separate-vanishing example and does not deny target-class membership of the same function.

One-degree base points do not establish poles of the limit. A base-locus example does not by itself exhibit a finite psh competitor, and loss of a twist estimate is a proof obstruction rather than a disproof.

The engine interface includes fixed-twist generation, equivariance and a nonzero starting sequence, beyond the formal five-item ideal package. Exhaustive hypothesis counts and unsupported novelty claims are removed.
